1.name: Moderate
1.summary: Normal activity; unusually sensitive people may shorten heavy outdoor exertion.

2.name: Sensitive
2.summary: Shorten intense outdoor exertion; sensitive groups keep windows shut at peak hours.

3.name: Unhealthy
3.summary: Reduce prolonged outdoor exertion; wear a well-fitted N95 on open transport.

4.name: Very unhealthy
4.summary: Avoid prolonged outdoor exertion; shut windows and run air filtration indoors.

5.name: Hazardous
5.summary: Avoid outdoor exertion; stay indoors with clean air and use N95 for essential trips.

shift_exercise_to_best_window.title: Shift outdoor exercise to cleanest window
shift_exercise_to_best_window.why: Breathing rates quadruple during jogging, so avoiding early-morning smog inversions sharply cuts inhaled dose.
steps: Check Today's strip before stepping out.
Keep high-effort intervals brief if level is Moderate or worse.

exercise_indoors_when_poor.title: Move exercise indoors on polluted days
exercise_indoors_when_poor.why: Indoor air filtered or shut away from traffic holds far less PM2.5 than street air at high breathing rates.
exercise_indoors_when_poor.when: Whenever Today's level reaches Unhealthy (L3) or higher.
steps: Use bodyweight mobility, yoga, or indoor stairs.
Run a purifier in the workout room if available.

n95_for_open_transport.title: Wear a fitted N95 / FFP2 on open commutes
n95_for_open_transport.why: Walkers, cyclists, two-wheelers, autos, and buses breathe near-outdoor concentrations along corridors.
n95_for_open_transport.when: For all open-air commutes and essential walks when level ≥ L3.
steps: Pinch the nose wire tightly so air passes through the filter, not gaps.
Replace the respirator when straps loosen or breathing resistance rises.

commute_to_public_transport.title: Shift private car/two-wheeler trips to bus or metro
commute_to_public_transport.why: Replaces private tailpipe CO2e and road NOx/PM, though open-air waiting/bus trips can raise personal exposure without a mask.
commute_to_public_transport.when: On regular work or college commute days.
steps: Pair bus or metro commutes with a fitted N95 on severe smog days.
Choose metro where available for lower cabin exposure and lower CO2e.

wfh_on_worst_day.title: Work or study from home on peak smog days
wfh_on_worst_day.why: Eliminates one round-trip commute in peak traffic emissions and keeps you inside cleaner filtered air.
wfh_on_worst_day.when: When Today's level is Very unhealthy (L4) or Hazardous (L5).
steps: Request remote work on Severe forecast days.
Keep doors and windows sealed during morning and evening rush hours.

no_idling.title: Turn off engine at signals and school gates
no_idling.why: Cutting 5 minutes/day of idling saves fuel, CO2e, and concentrated exhaust near children at school gates.
no_idling.when: At red lights, railway crossings, and pickup queues.
steps: Switch off ignition for waits longer than 30 seconds.
Park away from school entrance walkways when waiting.

errands_in_best_window.title: Batch outdoor errands into the cleanest window
errands_in_best_window.why: Midday boundary-layer mixing typically dilutes ground-level smoke compared with dawn and late evening.
steps: Combine grocery, pharmacy, and bank stops into one midday loop.
Avoid roadside waiting during peak evening hours.

child_play_indoors_when_poor.title: Keep children's play indoors on Unhealthy+ days
child_play_indoors_when_poor.why: Children breathe more air per kg of body weight and develop lungs are vulnerable to PM2.5.
child_play_indoors_when_poor.when: On all days rated Unhealthy (L3) through Hazardous (L5).
steps: Coordinate with school teachers to cancel outdoor PE on L4-L5 days.
Set up active indoor games away from kitchen smoke.

trip_chaining.title: Chain errands into existing commutes
trip_chaining.why: Combining stops trims total vehicle km by roughly 10% (5-15% range), cutting fuel burn and emissions.
trip_chaining.when: Across weekly car or two-wheeler trips.
steps: Plan weekly errands along your main commute route.
Avoid cold-start short solo drives under 2 km.

air_house_in_best_window.title: Air the house only in the cleanest 2-hour window
air_house_in_best_window.why: Cross-ventilating during the lowest PM2.5 hours refreshes CO2 without flooding rooms with peak smog.
air_house_in_best_window.when: Open opposite windows briefly around {bestStart}-{bestEnd} if below L4.
steps: Close windows promptly before evening inversion builds.
Keep windows shut all day if the best window stays L4+.

close_windows_at_peak.title: Shut windows during peak smog hours
close_windows_at_peak.why: Evening and early-morning temperature inversions trap smoke near ground level; sealing reduces penetration.
close_windows_at_peak.when: Before and throughout the avoid window ({avoidStart}-{avoidEnd}).
steps: Close balcony doors and kitchen exterior vents before dusk.
Turn off exhaust fans once cooking finishes so polluted air isn't pulled in.

run_purifier_through_night.title: Run your purifier continuously while at home
run_purifier_through_night.why: Nighttime outdoor PM2.5 peaks while you sleep for 8 hours; continuous filtration cuts overnight indoor levels.
run_purifier_through_night.when: All sleeping and indoor hours, especially 22:00-07:00.
steps: Keep bedroom door closed so the unit cleans a smaller air volume.
Set to a quiet medium speed overnight rather than turning it off.

diy_box_fan_filter.title: Build a taped MERV-13 / HEPA DIY box-fan filter
diy_box_fan_filter.why: A sealed box fan with a true high-MERV or replacement HEPA filter delivers substantial CADR at low cost.
diy_box_fan_filter.when: Run whenever bedrooms or living spaces are occupied.
steps: Tape all edge gaps securely so air passes through the filter media.
Run continuously on medium speed in the main sleeping room.

buy_hepa_purifier.title: Add a true HEPA air purifier in the main room
buy_hepa_purifier.why: Properly sized HEPA filtration (250+ m³/h CADR) provides the largest verified drop in indoor PM2.5 exposure.
buy_hepa_purifier.when: Run continuously in the bedroom or main living room.
steps: Match CADR to room size and avoid ionizer/ozone add-on modes.
Check pre-filter dust weekly and replace HEPA media per schedule.

seal_gaps_and_door_sweeps.title: Seal window cracks and add door sweeps
seal_gaps_and_door_sweeps.why: Reducing uncontrolled air exchange from leaky frames slows outdoor smog infiltration into bedrooms.
seal_gaps_and_door_sweeps.when: One-time low-cost weekend fix before peak winter weeks.
steps: Apply foam weatherstripping along loose sliding window tracks.
Fit rubber sweeps under main entrance and balcony doors.

cooking_ventilation.title: Ventilate kitchen while frying or tadka
cooking_ventilation.why: Cooking aerosols spike indoor PM2.5 inside apartments unless exhausted directly outdoors.
cooking_ventilation.when: During active stove use (morning and evening meals).
steps: Switch on chimney/exhaust fan and cover pans when simmering.
Shut interior doors between kitchen and sleeping rooms while cooking.

damp_mop_dont_sweep.title: Damp mop floors instead of dry sweeping
damp_mop_dont_sweep.why: Dry brooms resuspend settled fine dust and soot back into breathing height.
steps: Use a damp microfiber mop and wet cloth on sills.
Leave outdoor shoes at the entrance mat.

avoid_indoor_smoke_sources.title: Avoid indoor smoke (incense, mosquito coils, candles)
avoid_indoor_smoke_sources.why: In sealed winter rooms, a single stick of incense or mosquito coil sharply raises fine particle levels.
steps: Use window mesh screens or electric liquid/bat alternatives instead of coils.
Skip indoor agarbatti, dhoop, and scented candles while rooms are shut.

lpg_instead_of_biomass.title: Switch cooking from wood/coal/biomass to LPG
lpg_instead_of_biomass.why: Eliminating solid-fuel indoor smoke removes the single largest indoor PM2.5 source.
steps: Use LPG or clean electric stoves for indoor cooking.
If outdoor solid-fuel cooking occurs nearby, keep windows shut downwind.

induction_cooking.title: Shift high-use boiling/simmering to induction
induction_cooking.why: Removes indoor combustion byproducts from gas burners in tight winter rooms.
induction_cooking.when: Daily tea, boiling, and everyday cooking.
steps: Use an induction cooktop for water, dal, and slow simmering.
Continue venting oil smoke when frying.

warmth_without_burning.title: Stay warm without burning wood, coal, or trash
warmth_without_burning.why: Open bonfires and coal braziers create intense neighbourhood smog blankets at breathing height.
steps: Layer woollens indoors and use safe oil-filled or electric heating.
Never burn charcoal or angithi inside closed rooms (CO risk).

carpool_shared_ride.title: Carpool or share daily car commutes
carpool_shared_ride.why: Halves per-person car CO2e while retaining lower enclosed-cabin particle exposure on severe days.
steps: Pair with neighbours or colleagues along the same corridor.
Keep cabin climate control on recirculate in heavy traffic.

walk_or_cycle_short_trips.title: Walk or cycle short trips under 3 km on cleaner days
walk_or_cycle_short_trips.why: Eliminates cold-start tailpipe emissions on short hops, suppressed when air is Unhealthy (L3+).
walk_or_cycle_short_trips.when: Only when Today's level is Good, Moderate, or Sensitive (L0-L2).
steps: Prefer quieter side streets away from diesel arterials.
Switch back to enclosed transit or N95 when AQI rises to L3+.

community_no_burning.title: Organise a zero leaf/waste-burning pledge on your street
community_no_burning.why: A single smouldering leaf or garbage pile bathes an entire block in toxic winter smoke.
community_no_burning.when: Coordinate with security guards and sanitation staff this week.
steps: Share safe electric warming options for night guards.
Report open waste burning via municipal/GRAP clean-air helplines.

society_dust_and_diesel_audit.title: Run an RWA dust, sprinkling, and DG-set audit
society_dust_and_diesel_audit.why: Road dust, uncovered construction material, and poorly maintained diesel generators drive hyperlocal spikes.
society_dust_and_diesel_audit.when: Raise at the next RWA committee meeting using the Community Brief.
steps: Cover soil/sand piles and wet-sweep society driveways.
Service society DG sets and enforce clean emission norms.

share_community_brief.title: Print & share the one-page Community Brief
share_community_brief.why: Shared school and RWA action protects children and outdoor workers across the whole complex.
share_community_brief.when: Today — takes two minutes via the Community Brief view.
steps: Download or print the one-page PDF brief.
Post in your society WhatsApp group and school parent forum.

cloth_mask.title: Myth: Cloth or surgical masks block PM2.5 smog
cloth_mask.fact: Fact: Cloth and loose surgical masks leak around the edges and let microscopic 2.5 µm particles pass. Only a snug N95/FFP2 respirator filters effectively.

indoor_plants.title: Myth: Houseplants clean room air as well as a purifier
indoor_plants.fact: Fact: Controlled chamber studies show potted plants remove negligible PM2.5 at room scale — it would take dozens to hundreds of plants per square metre to match one small HEPA unit.

ozone_ionizer.title: Myth: Ionizers or ozone purifiers are safer 'filterless' cleaners
ozone_ionizer.fact: Fact: Ionizers and ozone generators can emit lung-irritating ozone and secondary ultrafine particles. Prefer mechanical HEPA or MERV-13 filtration.

air_freshener.title: Myth: Incense or aerosol air fresheners 'purify' stale indoor air
air_freshener.fact: Fact: Sprays, candles, and incense release fine particulate matter and VOCs, worsening indoor pollution behind closed winter windows.
